text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Analysts say the re-election of U.S. President Bill Clinton will herald a difficult period in U.S.-Turkish relations as he applies pressure on human rights, Cyprus and northern Iraq.
- Following rumours that he will resign, Interior Minister Mehmet Agar says he will discuss his future with Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller.
- Police break up a student protest against education authorities in Ankara.
- The capital markets board warns the Treasury about its decision to establish an account to pool funds from public companies.
- In talks with international banking associations Treasury officials disguise the Islamist-led coalition's economic policies.
- President Suleyman Demirel's visit to Germany bears fruit as German officials indicate support for Turkey's application to full membership of the European Union.
- Authorities are reluctant to investigate the circumstances of a car crash in which a leading security official and alleged crime boss died in the same car.
- Textile companies have ordered feasibility studies to look into the possibility of developing operations across Anatolia.
